open_points.subject: K-13 repository independence
open_points.text: “the kernel keeps every implementation's code in its own records and depends on no repository to run, admit or roll back” conflicts with A08 rule 6: “Before every send, the kernel reads the operation again” from the platform manifest at its configured repository revision.
open_points.question: Does repository independence apply only to obtaining implementation code, or must a run—including operation-node sends—continue without access to the manifest repository?
options: Only implementation execution, admission and rollback are repository-independent; operation sends still require the configured manifest.
All runs are repository-independent, so the manifest information needed for sends must be stored or snapshotted by the kernel.
Only function-only runs are repository-independent; flows containing operation nodes depend on the manifest repository.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the claim as limited to implementation code; operation sends still read the configured manifest as A08 requires.

open_points.subject: mcp listener and reverse-proxy boundary
open_points.text: “The proxy terminates TLS and is the only client of the kernel's listener, whose address the installation names and which the host does not expose otherwise” states a security condition, but no rule constrains `mcp_listen_address`, authenticates the proxy, checks exposure, or defines a refusal when the condition is false.
open_points.question: Is proxy-only access merely an operational precondition, or must the kernel enforce or validate it, and which configured listener addresses are acceptable?
options: It is solely a host deployment precondition; the kernel accepts any syntactically valid configured address.
The kernel accepts only a local listener such as loopback or a Unix-domain socket and refuses other addresses.
The kernel accepts broader addresses but authenticates the reverse proxy before accepting requests.
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a host deployment precondition and bind the configured address without attempting to verify that the proxy is its only client.
